front.title: AI Terms: Per-Use Terms, Payment and Receipts for Automated AI Access to Web Content

abstract.t: This document defines AI Terms: a JSON document published at the well-known URI /.well-known/ai-terms in which a website states, for each of four uses of its content by automated AI systems (search, answer, training and agent), whether the use is allowed, allowed for a price, or not allowed. Each use corresponds to one category of the IETF AI Preferences vocabulary, and the document defines how a site's terms are written, conservatively, as AI Preferences statements (the Content-Usage header field and robots.txt rule) for clients that read only those. AI Terms extends the AI Preferences work with what it leaves out: a price and a free allowance, a payment binding (HTTP 402, with x402 as the first), a purpose declaration by the client (the AI-Purpose header field), a description of a paid page that the payment depends on, and a receipt that records the use.
